name: Milky Way
summary: Our home galaxy, with 100–400 billion stars and a 4-million-solar-mass black hole at its centre.

name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
summary: The nearest large galaxy, visible to the naked eye; may merge with the Milky Way in ~4–5 billion years.

name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
summary: Third-largest Local Group galaxy.

name: Large Magellanic Cloud
summary: Satellite galaxy hosting the Tarantula Nebula and SN 1987A.

name: Small Magellanic Cloud
summary: Companion of the LMC, being torn apart.

name: Sagittarius Dwarf
summary: Being shredded by the Milky Way; its passages may have triggered spiral arms.

name: Whirlpool Galaxy (M51)
summary: Classic grand-design spiral tugging on a companion.

name: Sombrero Galaxy (M104)
summary: A bright bulge and dust lane like a hat; JWST showed its clumpy ring.

name: M87
summary: Home of the first black hole ever imaged (2019) and a 5,000-light-year jet.

name: Centaurus A
summary: The nearest active galaxy, with radio lobes a million light-years long.

name: Cartwheel Galaxy
summary: Shaped by a head-on collision with a smaller galaxy.

name: Antennae Galaxies
summary: Two galaxies colliding, igniting bursts of star formation.

name: Pinwheel Galaxy (M101)
summary: Hosted supernova SN 2023ixf, the closest in a decade.

name: Cigar Galaxy (M82)
summary: Forming stars 10× faster than the Milky Way, blowing out superwinds.

name: Hoag's Object
summary: An almost perfect ring galaxy of unknown origin.

name: IC 1101
summary: One of the largest galaxies known.

name: GN-z11
summary: Seen 400 million years after the Big Bang, with an active black hole.

name: JADES-GS-z14-0
summary: Confirmed at z = 14.3 (2024), about 290 million years after the Big Bang.

name: MoM-z14
summary: The most distant confirmed galaxy (z = 14.44), ~280 million years after the Big Bang (2025–26).

name: Dragonfly 44
summary: A galaxy thought to be mostly dark matter.

name: NGC 1052-DF2
summary: Appeared to have almost no dark matter.

name: Phoenix Cluster
summary: A cluster with a central galaxy forming stars at a record rate.

name: Bullet Cluster
summary: Colliding clusters whose separated mass and gas offer key evidence for dark matter.

name: El Gordo
summary: The largest known distant galaxy cluster.

name: Virgo Cluster
summary: Over 1,300 galaxies; centre of our Local Supercluster.

name: Laniakea Supercluster
summary: Our home supercluster (defined 2014), containing ~100,000 galaxies.

name: Hercules–Corona Borealis Great Wall
summary: Possibly the largest structure known in the universe.

name: Orion Nebula (M42)
summary: The nearest massive star-forming region, visible to the naked eye.

name: Pillars of Creation (Eagle Nebula)
summary: Iconic columns of gas imaged by Hubble (1995) and JWST (2022).

name: Crab Nebula (M1)
summary: Remains of the supernova recorded by Chinese astronomers in 1054.

name: Carina Nebula
summary: Home to Eta Carinae; its 'Cosmic Cliffs' were among JWST's first images.

name: Ring Nebula (M57)
summary: A dying Sun-like star's shell.

name: Helix Nebula
summary: The 'Eye of God', one of the nearest planetary nebulae.

name: Cat's Eye Nebula
summary: One of the most complex planetary nebulae.

name: Horsehead Nebula
summary: A dark dust cloud shaped like a horse's head.

name: Tarantula Nebula
summary: The most active starburst region in the Local Group.

name: Lagoon Nebula (M8)
summary: Bright naked-eye star nursery.

name: Veil Nebula
summary: Delicate filaments from a supernova ~10,000 years ago.

name: Cassiopeia A
summary: The youngest known Milky Way supernova remnant (~340 years).

name: Pleiades (M45)
summary: The Seven Sisters, a young cluster known to cultures worldwide (Krittika in India).

name: Omega Centauri
summary: The largest globular cluster, possibly the core of a swallowed galaxy, hosting an intermediate-mass black hole.

name: 47 Tucanae
summary: A dense ball of ~a million old stars.

name: Hyades
summary: The nearest open cluster.
